# Fortive's Post-Separation Portfolio Strategy: Segment Economics, Momentum, and Prioritization

## Executive summary

Fortive's June 28, 2025 spin-off of its Precision Technologies (PT) segment into Ralliant Corporation (one share of RAL per three FTV shares) converted the company from a three-segment conglomerate into a two-segment "New Fortive" — Intelligent Operating Solutions (IOS, ~70% of revenue) and Advanced Healthcare Solutions (AHS, ~30%) (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250630319069/en/Fortive-Announces-Completion-of-the-Ralliant-Separation-and-Appointment-of-Olumide-Soroye-as-President-CEO-and-Director-of-Fortive; https://investors.fortive.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001659166-25-000119/q22025-ex991.htm). The segment data show a clear hierarchy in both unit economics and trajectory: **IOS is the margin and earnings-quality anchor with improving trajectory; AHS is the higher-organic-growth but structurally lower-margin asset whose margin is being held flat while it invests; PT (now Ralliant) was the deteriorating asset — negative core growth and the largest margin compression — which is precisely why it was separated.** The separation appears to have strengthened the retained portfolio: on a like-for-like continuing-operations basis, New Fortive's adjusted operating margin expanded ~80 bps in Q1 2025, and full-year 2025 delivered a 110 bps adjusted EBITDA margin gain to 29.6% with IOS margins inflecting upward after the spin (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1659166/000165916626000003/q42025-ex991.htm).

## 1. Q2 2025 operating margins vs. full-year 2024

Two primary-source presentations exist for Q2 2025, and both should be noted. The 10-Q segment table for the quarter ended June 27, 2025 (which still included PT as a continuing segment) gives exact figures; the July 30, 2025 press release's "continuing operations" table (PT treated as discontinued for presentation) uses slightly different rounded segment figures (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1659166/000165916625000119/q22025-ex991.htm; segment table per the 10-Q reproduced in the same filing). FY2024 full-year margins come from the 2024 Form 10-K MD&A (https://grepcent.com/company/FTV/mda/fy2024/).

| Segment | Q2 2025 GAAP op margin (10-Q table) | Q2 2025 op margin (press release, cont. ops) | FY2024 GAAP op margin | Change vs FY2024 | Q2 2025 adj. EBITDA margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IOS | 24.7% ($166.7M / $675.7M) | 24.5% ($171M / $697M) | 26.0% ($704.6M / $2,714.7M) | −~130 bps (Q2-only basis) | 33.8% |
| PT (Ralliant) | 17.8% ($93.2M / $523.6M) | n/a (discontinued) | 22.4% ($500.0M / $2,229.4M) | −~460 bps | n/a |
| AHS | 12.2% ($39.1M / $319.5M) | 11.2% ($36M / $320M) | 12.1% ($155.6M / $1,287.7M) | ~+10–15 bps (flat) | 26.9% |

Verification arithmetic: IOS 166.7/675.7 = 24.7%; PT 93.2/523.6 = 17.8%; AHS 39.1/319.5 = 12.2%; FY24 IOS 704.6/2714.7 = 26.0%; PT 500.0/2229.4 = 22.4%; AHS 155.6/1287.7 = 12.1%. The small gap between the 10-Q table and the press-release "continuing operations" presentation (IOS 24.7% vs 24.5%; AHS 12.2% vs 11.2%) stems from the release's rounded headline figures and the Ralliant-as-discontinued cost allocation; the difference does not change the ranking or conclusions.

Interpretation of unit economics: **IOS is decisively the strongest business** — its GAAP margin is more than double AHS's and ~7 points above PT's at Q2 2025, and on an adjusted EBITDA basis (which strips acquisition amortization that is unusually heavy in AHS and IOS software) IOS runs at 33.8% vs 26.9% for AHS. The Q2-to-FY margin comparison must be read carefully: Q2 is seasonally Fortive's softest margin quarter, so IOS's Q2 2025 24.7% sitting below the FY2024 26.0% average does not indicate deterioration — Q4 2025 came in at 27.6% and the full-year 2025 margin rose to 25.8% (+50 bps YoY on a comparable continuing-ops basis). AHS is the only segment whose Q2 2025 margin roughly matched its 2024 full-year level (12.2% vs 12.1%), i.e., flat unit economics despite revenue softness. PT is the clear laggard: margin collapsed from 22.4% (FY2024, itself flattered ~285 bps by a gain on sale of land/buildings) to 17.8% in Q2 2025, and to 17.4% in Q1 2025 (https://investors.fortive.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001659166-25-000079/q12025-ex991.htm).

## 2. Revenue growth momentum, 2023 → 2024

From the FY2024 10-K segment data (https://grepcent.com/company/FTV/mda/fy2024/):

| Segment | FY2023 revenue | FY2024 revenue | Reported growth | Core growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IOS | $2,612.2M | $2,714.7M | **+3.9%** | +3.4% |
| PT | $2,223.7M | $2,229.4M | +0.3% | **−3.7%** |
| AHS | $1,229.4M | $1,287.7M | **+4.7%** | **+6.1%** |

Momentum pattern: AHS had the fastest organic growth (6.1% core, driven by sterilization and dosimetry volume plus ~price), IOS had steady mid-single-digit-type core growth (3.4%, driven by gas detection, SaaS/facility-asset software, and favorable pricing), and PT was the weakest — its reported +0.3% was entirely an artifact of the $1.72B EA Elektro-Automatik acquisition (+4.4% contribution) masking a 3.7% organic decline in test & measurement and industrial sensing. This divergence widened in 2025: Q1 2025 core growth was IOS +2%, AHS +2.5%, PT −8.4% (https://exa.ai/library/markets/stocks/FTV/earnings/FY2025/Q1/transcript). So growth leadership (AHS) and margin leadership (IOS) sat with the retained segments, while the spun-off PT segment combined negative organic growth with deteriorating margins — the "worst of both" profile that motivated the separation.

## 3. Overall operating margin trend: Q1 2025 vs Q1 2024

Consolidated GAAP operating margin fell from 19.8% (Q1 2024, $302.2M operating profit on $1,524.5M sales) to 15.8% (Q1 2025, $233.6M on $1,474.2M) — a 400 bps decline on the reported basis (10-Q segment tables in https://investors.fortive.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001659166-25-000079/q12025-ex991.htm). That headline drop is misleading in both directions and is explained by three mix/comparability effects:

1. Q1 2024 included a $63.1M gain on sale of property in PT (≈4 points of the margin), which did not repeat.
2. PT's own margin collapsed YoY (26.7% → 17.4%), dragging the consolidated figure.
3. On the adjusted basis management uses to run the business, **operating margin expanded 20 bps YoY to 25.3%** in Q1 2025, "led by strong performance in Intelligent Operating Solutions"; on a New Fortive continuing-operations basis (IOS + AHS combined), adjusted operating margins expanded ~80 bps YoY with IOS adjusted margins up 150 bps to 33.3% (https://investors.fortive.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001659166-25-000079/q12025-ex991.htm; https://in.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-fortives-q1-2025-results-meet-eps-expectations-stock-dips-93CH-4804202).

The trajectory through and after the separation confirms the improvement: Q2 2025 continuing-ops adjusted EBITDA margin 28.4% (−20 bps YoY on soft revenue), Q3 30.1% (+10.4% YoY growth), Q4 31.9% (+90 bps), full-year 2025 29.6% (+110 bps), with FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $2.90–$3.00 initiated (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1659166/000165916626000003/q42025-ex991.htm; https://investors.fortive.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001659166-25-000129/q32025-ex991.htm).

## 4. What this reveals about portfolio prioritization

**IOS is the designated value engine.** At the June 2025 Investor Day, management positioned New Fortive around ~50% recurring revenue, a 4% five-year core growth CAGR, ~64% adjusted gross margin, ~29% adjusted EBITDA margin, and ~$0.9B free cash flow, with IOS explicitly described as "~70% of FTV revenue" (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/fortive-presentation-pdf-q2-2025-ce7c5fdfda80fe2c; https://investors.fortive.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/267/fortive-to-outline-value-creation-strategy-and-financial-framework). The operating data support that hierarchy: IOS contributes ~70% of segment operating profit, carries the best margin (24.5–24.7% GAAP; 33.8% adj. EBITDA in Q2; 35.1% for FY2025, +110 bps), and is where the durable growth vectors live (Fluke software/services ARR growing double digits, facility & asset lifecycle SaaS, connected worker safety). FY2025 results show IOS margin expansion accelerated post-spin: GAAP 25.8% (+50 bps), Q4 27.6%, adj. EBITDA 37.4% in Q4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1659166/000165916626000003/q42025-ex991.htm).

**AHS is the growth asset being run for investment, not yet margin.** It posted the fastest core growth (6.1% in 2024) but structurally the lowest margins (GAAP ~12%, dragged by ~14% of sales in amortization; adjusted EBITDA ~26–27%), and its 2025 margin slipped ~20 bps as management made "localized growth investments" and SaaS conversions (Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin 26.0%, −150 bps YoY). The prioritization is explicit: AHS growth and recurring-revenue conversion take precedence over near-term margin (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/02/04/fortive-ftv-q4-2025-earnings-call-transcript/). Its 59% adjusted gross margin and consumables/SaaS mix give it option value, but it is not yet the margin story.

**PT was separated precisely because it was the lagging asset.** On separation criteria — cyclicality (test & measurement order delays), negative organic growth (−3.7% in 2024, −8.4% in Q1 2025), margin compression (−210 bps in 2024, −460 bps by Q2 2025 vs FY24), and capital intensity (the $1.72B EA acquisition and heavy deal-related amortization) — PT was the portfolio's margin and momentum problem, not its engine. Management's own framing at the September 2024 announcement was that Fortive would become "more focused on recurring revenue and software businesses, and better positioned to accelerate growth," while Ralliant would "focus on powerful secular growth trends" as a standalone with its own capital-return model (https://investors.fortive.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/242/fortive-announces-strategic-plans-for-separation-into-two-independent-public-companies).

**The separation strengthened the retained units' competitive positioning.** Evidence: (1) New Fortive received ~$1.0B net cash consideration from Ralliant (https://investors.fortive.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001659166-25-000104/ex992-unauditedproformasta.htm), funding $1.6B of share repurchases in FY2025 (~26M shares, ~8% of diluted shares, in 2H alone) — capital that lifts per-share economics for the retained businesses; (2) margin mix improved immediately — the adjusted operating margin rose 20 bps YoY in Q1 2025 on a deteriorating reported base, and continuing-ops adjusted EBITDA margin rose 110 bps for FY2025 to 29.6%; (3) growth re-accelerated post-spin — Q4 2025 reported revenue +4.6%/core +3.3%, the first quarter with volume growth returning, and IOS core +4%; (4) the "Fortive Accelerated" strategy (FBS Amplified, disciplined capital allocation, investor trust) produced double-digit recurring revenue growth outpacing consolidated growth and a raised FY2025 guidance (https://investors.fortive.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001659166-25-000129/q32025-ex991.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1659166/000165916626000003/q42025-ex991.htm).

## 5. Bottom line

- **Strongest unit economics and trajectory: IOS.** It is the only segment that pairs a top-quartile margin (24.7% Q2 2025 GAAP; 33.8% adjusted EBITDA; 35.1% FY2025) with consistently positive core growth (3.4% in 2024; 2–4% through 2025) and accelerating margin expansion after the spin (+50 bps GAAP, +110 bps adjusted EBITDA in FY2025). Its Q2 2025 margin dip versus the FY2024 average is seasonal, not structural — Q4 2025 hit 27.6%.
- **AHS** has the fastest organic growth (6.1% core, 2023–24) but structurally lowest margins (12.2% Q2 2025 GAAP, ~flat vs 12.1% FY2024; 26.9% adjusted EBITDA) and is deliberately being run for growth/recurring-conversion investment, with margins flat-to-slightly-down.
- **PT/Ralliant** was the weakest on both dimensions (core −3.7% in 2024; margin down ~460 bps by Q2 2025) — the separation divested the margin/momentum drag.
- The retained portfolio's overall margin trend (adjusted operating margin +20 bps in Q1 2025 despite reported GAAP falling 400 bps on one-off and mix effects; continuing-ops adjusted EBITDA margin 29.6% in FY2025, +110 bps) indicates the separation improved mix, freed ~$1B of cash for buybacks, and left IOS — the strongest business — as the unambiguous strategic center of gravity. Uncertainty caveats: Q2 2025 vs FY2024 comparisons mix a seasonal quarter against an annual average; the press-release "continuing operations" margin figures differ slightly from 10-Q segment tables due to rounding and discontinued-ops cost allocation; and PT's FY2024 margin was inflated by a one-time property gain, so its underlying deterioration was even steeper than the headline numbers show.

At 1% risk per trade = $7/trade. To make $200/week with $7 risk per trade... even at generous 2:1 R:R, each win = $14. Need ~14-15 wins/week net. That's 3-4 trades/day. And $7 risk budget can't even buy one contract of anything — minimum option price typically $0.05 → $5 per contract, meaning most single-leg options with real liquidity cost $1.00+ = $100/contract. Let me compute what risk per trade would be required. Suppose risk R dollars per trade, and the target is $250/week. Under the "risk of ruin" framework, the required risk per trade to average $250/week from $700.

Let's say a trader takes 5 trades/week (one per day). Expectancy per trade = $50. If win rate 50% and R:R = 1:1, expectancy = 0. So need positive expectancy. With R:R of 2:1 (win = 2R, loss = R) and win rate p: expectancy = p(2R) - (1-p)R = R(3p - 1). For expectancy $50 with 5 trades/week, need 3p-1 = 50/(5R) → p = (1 + 10/R)/3.
